text: Onions and garlic are ubiquitous in cuisines around the world, serving as essential flavorings that elevate dishes with their robust, umami-rich aromas. Onions, with their bulbous shape and varied colors from red to brown, are a staple in European, Latin American, Asian, and many Middle Eastern cooking traditions, lending a rich, sweet flavor with a hint of sharpness that cuts through fats and complements a multitude of meats and vegetables. Garlic, in its numerous forms—fresh, dried, powdered, and fermented—as well as in its multiple allium relatives like chives and leeks, is an indispensable ingredient in Italian, Spanish, Chinese, Indian, and countless other culinary landscapes. These humble yet powerful plants have become so ingrained in the culinary arts that they are often considered the unsung heroes of flavor, perfectly blending into and elevating any dish they grace.
summary: onions and garlic in every cuisine.
